key_insight: Rapids co-designs a streaming neural decoder with FPGA hardware to deliver fast, accurate quantum error correction while making classical compute a scalable resource.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware decoding can meet superconducting processors’ rapid syndrome cycles without sacrificing accuracy, potentially reducing the physical-qubit overhead of fault tolerance.
method: Stream syndrome measurements through a neural decoder.
Use FPGA-efficient operations and train in the device’s integer arithmetic.
Scale across multiple FPGAs or implement the design in custom silicon.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports under 1 microsecond per syndrome round for a distance-19 surface code on one FPGA, a 240-fold lower logical error rate than existing real-time hardware decoders, and 16-fold higher accuracy than Relay on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code.
watch_item: Per-round throughput does not establish end-to-end decision latency; deployment should verify latency and accuracy under device-specific noise and integration constraints.
paper_title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
